claims.text: Cast or conventionally annealed MPEAs such as CoCrFeMnNi or Al-containing variants have a coarse-grained, single-phase FCC or BCC structure.
The initial MPEA state has a low dislocation density.
The initial MPEA is brittle at room temperature because of limited slip-system activation or grain-boundary embrittlement.
Room-temperature HPT or ECAP will refine the alloy to the submicron or nanocrystalline regime.
SPD followed by short sub-recrystallization annealing will produce a hierarchical nanograin-in-matrix structure with a dislocation density of approximately 10^15 m^-2.
Short low-temperature annealing after SPD will form coherent nanoscale solute-rich clusters or precipitates without significant grain growth.
The treatment will increase the fraction of low-energy grain boundaries.
The coherent nanoscale precipitates will act as both dislocation sources and dislocation barriers.
SPD-generated geometrically necessary dislocations and grain boundaries will raise yield strength through grain-refinement and Hall–Petch strengthening.
The short anneal will relax internal stresses while retaining the refined grain structure.
High-density grain-boundary dislocation sources will enable uniform plastic deformation and improve ductility.
Coherent precipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent precipitate interfaces relieve stress concentrations that could otherwise cause premature crack initiation.
The combined precipitates and refined grains will preserve high strength while dislocation transmission and source activation improve ductility.
The SPD-plus-annealing route will increase yield strength by more than 30% relative to the initial state.
The SPD-plus-annealing route will increase uniform tensile elongation by more than 15% relative to the initial state.
The treated alloy will have significantly greater total energy absorption than both the initial brittle state and standard annealed states.
Standard solution annealing and slow cooling typically produce coarse grains and low dislocation density.
Standard annealing or conventional precipitation hardening exhibits a strength–ductility trade-off, with coarse precipitates causing premature void nucleation in the strengthened condition.
The proposed route is most applicable to moderate-SFE MPEAs and may fail when twinning dominates, grain growth occurs, or brittle intermetallics form.

contradictions.description: The conventionally annealed initial state is characterized as highly brittle, while the standard solution-annealed baseline is characterized as having high ductility and low strength. The hypothesis does not explain whether these are different annealing conditions or different alloy subclasses.

The falsification threshold refers to grain growth greater than twice the 'initial grain size,' but the defined initial state is coarse-grained whereas the relevant pre-anneal state after SPD is nanocrystalline. Taken literally, this threshold would not detect substantial post-SPD grain growth unless 'initial' is redefined as the SPD-only state.
